claims.text: Elevated-temperature oxidizing conditions cause the eutectic high-entropy alloy to form a mixed-metal oxide scale.
The mixed-metal oxide scale is protective against corrosion when it remains intact.
The mixed-metal oxide scale is brittle or fragile under cyclic mechanical loading.
Cyclic mechanical wear repeatedly spalls or removes the oxide scale.
Removal of the oxide scale exposes fresh, highly reactive alloy surface.
The newly exposed alloy surface corrodes rapidly in the stated environment.
Repeated oxide formation and mechanical removal synergistically increases corrosion.
Repeated oxide formation and mechanical removal synergistically increases wear-related material removal.
Simultaneous wear and corrosion at 500–550 °C will produce greater total degradation than static corrosion with minimal wear under otherwise matched conditions.
The simultaneous wear-corrosion condition will produce deeper wear scars than the static-corrosion baseline.
The simultaneous wear-corrosion condition will produce greater corrosion depth than the static-corrosion baseline.
Minimal mechanical wear permits formation of a more stable oxide layer than cyclic mechanical wear.
The proposed mechanism operates under oxidizing conditions at 500–550 °C where oxide formation is possible.
The proposed coupled-degradation effect should diminish in non-oxidizing environments.
The proposed coupled-degradation effect should diminish at lower temperatures where oxide formation is suppressed.
Variations in oxide composition, brittleness, and mechanical loading sensitivity may alter the quantitative degradation rate.
